### REQ-015: WiFi reconnection must never give up

- **Status:** DONE
- **Added:** 2026-07-02
- **Completed:** 2026-07-04
- **Verified by:** code review + idf.py build 2026-07-04 (no hardware attached; AP-outage test pending)
- **Depends on:** –
- **Description:**

`WiFiManager::startReconnectTimer()` (`net/wifi_manager.cpp:201-214`) stops scheduling reconnect attempts after `CONFIG_THERMO_WIFI_MAX_RETRY` (default 10) tries at `CONFIG_THERMO_WIFI_RECONNECT_INTERVAL` (default 5 s). `retryCount_` is only reset on a successful IP. Any AP outage longer than ~50 s therefore leaves the device **permanently offline until power-cycled**. The legacy firmware (`src/main.cpp:83-98`, `KeepWiFiConnected()`) retried WiFi and MQTT forever — this is a migration regression and the top availability risk for a building-wide fleet.

Fix: retry indefinitely; use the attempt counter only for exponential backoff (e.g. 5 s doubling to a 60–120 s cap) to avoid hammering the AP. Log a warning at each backoff step.

See finding F-3 in `doc/reports/2026-07-02_migration_code_review.md`.

- **Acceptance criteria:**
  - [ ] Device reconnects automatically after an AP outage longer than `MAX_RETRY × interval` (test: disable AP for 5+ minutes, re-enable, device rejoins without reset) — *pending, no board attached 2026-07-04*
  - [x] Backoff capped (5 s doubling to 120 s cap — no faster than 1 attempt/s, no slower than 1 attempt/2 min)
  - [ ] MQTT reconnects automatically after WiFi returns (existing esp-mqtt auto-reconnect verified end-to-end) — *pending, no board attached 2026-07-04*
  - [x] Kconfig option semantics updated or removed (`THERMO_WIFI_MAX_RETRY` removed; reconnect interval help text documents backoff)
- **Notes:** Heating control continues offline (PID keeps running on local sensors), so the only loss during outage is reporting/commands — but only if reconnection eventually succeeds.
